thread:
Ellen: Quick spike idea - introduce a 'staged commit token' for config changes. Instead of flip/rollback, you produce a token that represents a validated checkpoint. Tokens can be promoted, chained, or revoked. Means we can audit exact state that passed gates.

Marco: Hmm, a token sounds like a lightweight snapshot id. How would it be minted? Who signs it? :thinking_face:

Ellen: Implementation sketch: config apply -> simulate/dry-run -> run gates -> if pass, mint token: e.g., token: token:CFG::2026-03-22::sim-9012::sha256=abc123. Token metadata stored in audit log + reference in the config object.

Priyanka: Love auditability. A few thoughts: 1) token should include gate params and metrics snapshot (not huge, just summed deltas), 2) tokens need TTL & revocation list, 3) must be verifiable off-line by security.

Marco: Operational semantics: when you 'promote' a token, the system only applies diffs from last-promoted-token, and will refuse to apply if local cluster state diverged. That prevents blind overwrites.

Ellen: Exactly. Also helpful for safe rollbacks: we can 'revert-to-token' which applies the last known-good state. Revert semantics should be additive: we produce a new token for the revert so history is preserved.

Priyanka: UX: Console change list should show tokens in timeline with pass/fail badges, who minted them, and a small "verify" button that fetches stored metric snapshot. Add a warning for stale tokens (older than 30d).

Marco: Gate integration: token minted only after gate pass. For failing gates, still create a draft token with status 'failed' so teams can iterate. Draft tokens are not promotable.

ops-bot: simulation-runner: sim-9012 completed (mode: shadow, sample: 0.01) -> gates: pass(error_rate,p95) -> token minted token:CFG::2026-03-22::sim-9012::sha256=abc123.

audit-bot: audit entry created: token:CFG::2026-03-22::sim-9012::sha256=abc123 by Ellen (team: infra) at 6133334458.

Ellen: API sketch (single-line json in message): POST /api/v1/config/commit -> {"token":"token:CFG::2026-03-22::sim-9012::sha256=abc123","promote":true,"cooldown":600} The promote call will verify current cluster-state 'base-token' matches token.base_reference and will apply diffs.

Priyanka: Security: add signed attestations optional via KMS so customers can require signed tokens for private deploys. Also add role 'token-revoker'.

Marco: Edge cases: 1) if a token's metric_snapshot references a dataset that's been purged we should mark token unverifiable and require manual review, 2) chained tokens may conflict if overlapping diffs exist; define conflict resolution: reject promote with conflict report.

Ellen: Telemetry hooks: emit events token.minted, token.promoted, token.revoked with token id, user, gate result, and a short summary string. Those go to Console's timeline and to BI for weekly audits.

Priyanka: I can draft the token format and TTL policy. Also propose default: token TTL=90d, auto-mark-stale=30d, replay-power required to verify older tokens.

Marco: Dev-experience: add CLI helpers: `rictl config mint-token --change ... --simulate --output-token` and `rictl config promote --token <id>`. CLI returns a short human-readable diff and a machine-readable exit code.

Ellen: Next steps: 1) Priyanka write token spec + revocation model, 2) Marco prototype CLI changes, 3) add telemetry event schema, 4) UX mock for token timeline. Who wants the RFC?

Priyanka: I'll own the RFC. Will include token JSON schema (flat string fields), audit examples, and a sample KMS attestation flow.

Marco: I'll prototype CLI and the base-token pre-checks. Ping me if you want a pairing session.

Ellen: Great. I'll add a task to the rollout RFC and flag this for the next ops sync. :thumbsup:
